# MCP Server Ecosystem

Covers vendor-maintained vs community servers, maturity, registries, and notable servers.

## Official Registry

The official MCP registry launched as a preview on September 8, 2025 at `registry.modelcontextprotocol.io` [18]. It is designed as the "primary source of truth" for MCP server discovery, with downstream sub-registries (client marketplaces, private enterprise registries) building upon it [18].

Key characteristics [18]:
- Open source with permissive licensing and OpenAPI specification
- Governed by a registry working group (lead: David Soria Parra)
- Community-driven moderation: members can flag violations; maintainers can denylist entries
- Preview release — no data durability guarantees; breaking changes possible before GA

## Registry Landscape

At least 7 separate MCP registries/directories exist in the ecosystem (from discovery agent findings):
- **Official MCP Registry**: registry.modelcontextprotocol.io [18]
- **Anthropic MCP Registry**: api.anthropic.com/mcp-registry (visible in Claude Code source [22])
- **GitHub MCP Registry**: integrated into VS Code Copilot [31]
- **Smithery**: commercial marketplace with OAuth infrastructure and server hosting
- **Glama**: hosted execution model with API gateway approach
- Additional community directories (awesome-mcp-servers lists on GitHub)

This fragmentation — 7+ registries within ~18 months of launch — suggests rapid but potentially chaotic ecosystem growth.

## Vendor-Maintained Servers

The official `modelcontextprotocol/servers` repository on GitHub contains reference implementations, explicitly labeled as educational examples rather than production-ready solutions (from discovery agent findings).

Initial servers shipped with the launch [8]: Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Git, Postgres, Puppeteer.

## Adoption

Early adopters at launch (November 2024) [8]: Block, Apollo, Zed, Replit, Codeium, Sourcegraph.

Subsequent adoption [7]:
- March 2025: OpenAI integrated MCP across products (ChatGPT desktop)
- April 2025: Google DeepMind announced adoption
- Microsoft: Semantic Kernel integration, Azure OpenAI
- December 2025: Governance transferred to AAIF (Linux Foundation), co-founded by Anthropic, Block, and OpenAI

## Production Readiness Assessment

There is a sharp divide between official positioning (reference servers are "educational examples") and practitioner claims of production readiness (from discovery agent findings).

Enterprise concerns identified across multiple sources:
- Audit trails and access revocation [13]
- OAuth security and sensitive data filtering [15]
- Prompt injection protection [13]
- Gateway control plane pattern recommended "from day one" (from discovery agent findings)

Mixed consensus: some servers (PostgreSQL, filesystem, SQLite) considered production-ready for specific use cases, while critical gaps exist in security architecture, data governance, and compliance.
